findings.body: Compilation fails: there is no no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() method; the only definition introduced is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm, so the call cannot be resolved.
findings.failure_mode: The module fails to build, so no downstream review or test can execute.
findings.impact: Compilation fails: there is no no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() method; the only definition introduced is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm, so the call cannot be resolved.
findings.root_cause: The added guard invokes isConditionalPasskeysEnabled with an arity that does not match the newly declared single-parameter method.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the user, e.g. `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, to match the declared signature isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel).
findings.title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments
findings.trigger: Compiling the services module after this patch is applied.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` call with no arguments at line 47 in UsernameForm.java, but the only method defined in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires one parameter. The literal search confirms the no-arg call exists only at UsernameForm.java:47 while all other calls pass `context.getUser()`. This is a compilation error introduced by the patch.

raw_findings.body: The old else-branch call that ran webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when the user was not yet selected is replaced by a single call guarded by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which is false when user==null; the webauthn/conditional-UI attributes are never set, so the passkey form (#webauth) is not rendered and discoverable/passkey login on the initial page no longer works, contradicting the assertions in the added tests that expect the webauth form present while user==null.
raw_findings.evidence: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime regression: passkey login page rendered without webauthn data for unidentified users.
raw_findings.impact: The old else-branch call that ran webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) when the user was not yet selected is replaced by a single call guarded by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which is false when user==null; the webauthn/conditional-UI attributes are never set, so the passkey form (#webauth) is not rendered and discoverable/passkey login on the initial page no longer works, contradicting the assertions in the added tests that expect the webauth form present while user==null.
raw_findings.root_cause: The relocated webauthn setup is guarded by a helper that adds a user!=null requirement, inverting the previous condition that set up webauthn precisely when the user was null.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the `&& user != null` constraint (or otherwise ensure fillContextForm is still invoked when the user is not yet identified) so the form is set up for both the initial and re-authentication cases.
raw_findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, dropping passkey form setup on the initial (unidentified) login page
raw_findings.trigger: A user opens the login page with passkeys enabled before being identified, so context.getUser() is null (idless/discoverable-key or first-time login).

finding.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, dropping passkey form setup on the initial (unidentified) login page
finding.trigger: A user opens the login page with passkeys enabled before being identified, so context.getUser() is null (idless/discoverable-key or first-time login).
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that passkey form setup is broken when user==null is incorrect. Looking at UsernamePasswordForm.java:115-117, `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` returns false when user is null (due to `&& user != null`), but this only guards the `fillContextForm` call. The candidate misunderstands the logic - when user is null, the code falls through to line 118-119 which still calls `challenge(context, formData)`. The WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm handles null users via shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators check. The test assertions mentioned are not contradicted by this logic.
